Metadata.title: Taka Sats | Verified Recycling. Bitcoin Paid.
Metadata.description: Taka Sats verifies recycling work, links field evidence and enables transparent Bitcoin payouts for collection teams, even when connectivity is limited.
Metadata.shareImageAlt: Taka Sats: verified recycling work with transparent Bitcoin payouts

Home.eyebrow: Open source · Offline first · Bitcoin Lightning
Home.description: Taka Sats lets a collection team identify collectors, weigh material, photograph the scale and pay in Bitcoin, with a record anyone can check.
Home.pointEvidence: A photo with every weigh in
Home.pointLedger: A ledger nobody can quietly edit
Home.sampleNote: Sample data. Demo mode: no real money moves.
Home.chipSavedBody: Sends itself when the signal returns.
Home.audienceTitle: One record. Three people who need to trust it.
Home.audienceCollectorBody: Get paid for a weight that was written down, into a wallet you control. No bank account, no ID document, no special app.
Home.audienceStaffBody: Decide who can be weighed and paid, see anything unusual, and compare what was collected with what the recycler accepted.
Home.audienceFunderBody: Check the totals and the ledger yourself with a free script. You see numbers, not people.
Home.flowTitle: From the collection line to the ledger.
Home.flowDescription: The field team follows a short guided flow. Underneath, identity, evidence, checks and payment stay connected.
Home.flowIdentifyDescription: Find an approved collector by name, public code or QR. Nobody pending can be weighed.
Home.flowWeighDescription: Pick the material and key in the scale reading. The rate in force is applied for you.
Home.flowEvidenceDescription: The photo's fingerprint is sealed into the record with the time, session and location.
Home.flowSyncDescription: Saved on the phone first. When online, each record is checked and added to the ledger.
Home.flowPayoutDescription: The person who recorded it cannot approve it. The sats go to the collector's verified wallet.
Home.screenFindSearch: Name, code or scan a QR
Home.screenProofHint: Show the material and the scale display.
Home.screenPayRule: You are a different person, so you can approve.
Home.screenPaid: Paid. Receipt saved to the ledger.
Home.trustEyebrow: Why you can trust the numbers
Home.trustTitle: Checks that do not depend on one person.
Home.trustIntro: No single check is enough, so there are several. Each one makes cheating slower, more visible or more expensive.
Home.trust1Body: A staff member vets each collector before any weigh in or payment.
Home.trust2Title: The photo is sealed to the weight
Home.trust2Body: The scale photo's fingerprint is part of the signed record, so a swapped photo shows.
Home.trust3Body: Whoever records a weigh in can never approve its payout.
Home.trust4Body: Kilograms collected are compared with kilograms the recycler accepted, and gaps are flagged for review.
Home.ledgerCaption: Each entry holds the fingerprint of the one before it. Change any past entry and every later link breaks. Anyone can check this with a free script.
Home.runBody: Taka Sats is free software under the AGPL licence. Host it on a small server, set your currency, language and rates in a settings file, and pay through any Lightning wallet provider that meets the published requirements.
Home.runPoint1Body: One small server and Docker. Your data stays with you.
Home.runPoint2Body: The hot wallet and the multisig pool that funds it are both pluggable.
Home.runPoint3Body: A programme in another city changes a file, not the software.
Home.ctaDescription: Supervisors and staff can sign in to the pilot.
Home.footer: Open infrastructure for verified recycling work and transparent Bitcoin payouts.

About.metaDescription: What Taka Sats is, why Afribit Africa is building it, and how every collection and payment is checked.
About.title: Pay people fairly for recycling. Keep an honest record.
About.lead: Taka Sats is free, open source software that lets a recycling programme weigh what collectors bring in, check it, and pay them in Bitcoin. Anyone can inspect the record of what was collected and what was paid.
About.problemTitle: Real work that is hard to prove
About.problemBody: Collecting recyclables is real work, but it is rarely recorded properly. Weights are written on paper or remembered. Payment comes late, in cash, or is disputed. Collectors have no proof of what they delivered, and the people who fund a programme have no proof that it happened.
About.step1Body: Staff look the person up by name or code. Each collector is approved by a staff member before they can be paid.
About.step2Title: The material is weighed and photographed
About.step2Body: The weight comes from a scale. A photo shows the material, the scale and its display. The phone saves everything, even with no internet.
About.step3Body: When the phone reconnects, the record is sealed so it cannot be changed quietly. The system checks the rate, the session, the supervisor and the photo, and flags anything unusual.
About.step4Body: A second person approves the payment. The sats go to the collector's own wallet. Nobody chooses the destination at payout time.
About.bitcoinBody: A collector does not need a bank account, an ID document or a special app to be paid. Payments over Lightning arrive in seconds and cost very little. A wallet the collector controls cannot be frozen by us or by anyone else. And every payment can be checked by people outside the programme.
About.openBody: Taka Sats runs on open standards. The code is free to read, copy and run under the AGPL licence, so any programme can host its own. By default collectors keep their own keys and the programme never holds money that belongs to a collector. We do not ask for ID numbers. Partners and funders see totals, not people.
About.honest1: Every collector is approved by staff first.
About.honest2: Weights come from a physical scale, with a photo as evidence.
About.honest3: Each record is sealed on the phone, so any edit is visible.
About.honest4: Repeated photos, repeated weights and unusual weights are flagged for review.
About.honest5: During the pilot, every payment needs a second person's approval.
About.honest6: What we paid for is compared with what the recycler accepted.
About.honest7: The ledger can be verified by anyone, so changed records show up.
About.statusBody: Taka Sats is ready for a supervised pilot. For now it runs in demo mode, which means payments are simulated and no real money moves. Before any real payment we will test with small amounts and a named group of staff.
About.whoBody: Taka Sats is built for Afribit Africa and designed so that other recycling and circular economy programmes can run it too. It is open source, so you can read every line, ask questions and help improve it.
About.footer: Taka Sats is open source software under the AGPL-3.0 licence.

payouts.intro: Every collection becomes a payout. A second person approves it, then the worker pays. Nobody pays by hand.

payouts.approveHint: You cannot approve a collection you recorded yourself.
payouts.retryConfirm: Retry this payout? Check the wallet first: a retry can pay twice if the first attempt actually landed.

payouts.openEvent: Open the collection and its checks

treasury.dutyOther: {count, plural, one {# more approval} other {# more approvals}} needed. Your approval counts once.

treasury.arrived: The funds arrived. Waiting payouts were woken.

events.title: Collections
events.intro: Every weigh that reached the server. Open one to see how we know it happened as claimed.
events.flags: {count, plural, one {# open flag} other {# open flags}}
events.detailIntro: Each line below is a question the system answered from stored facts. A warning is a note for a person, not a block.

collector_authorized.label: Was the collector authorized?
collector_authorized.pass: Yes. The collector is authorized now, and the server refuses events from collectors that are not.

session_window.label: Was it recorded inside the session window?
session_window.pass: Yes. The session ran {start} to {end}, with {grace} minutes of grace.
session_window.fail: No. The session ran {start} to {end}, with {grace} minutes of grace.

rate_in_force.label: Was the signed rate the one in force?
rate_in_force.pass: Yes. The rate on the event ({rate} per kg) was the active rate at the moment of recording.
rate_in_force.fail: No. A different rate was active when this was recorded.
rate_in_force.unknown: No rate could be found for that material and time.

photo_stored.label: Did the scale photo arrive?
photo_stored.pass: Yes. The photo is stored under its fingerprint.
photo_stored.warn: Not yet. Photos upload on their own and can arrive after the event.

gps_inside.label: Was the phone inside the session boundary?
gps_inside.pass: Yes. The fix is inside the boundary.
gps_inside.fail: No. The fix is outside the session boundary.
gps_inside.warn: There was no location fix. The supervisor gave this reason: {reason}
gps_inside.unknown: The session has no boundary, so the fix cannot be judged.

duplicate_photo.label: Was this photo used before?
duplicate_photo.pass: No sign of a reused photo.
duplicate_photo.fail: A reviewer confirmed the same photo was filed on another collection.
duplicate_photo.warn: The same photo was filed on an earlier collection. Review the flag.

weight_outlier.label: Is the weight unusual for this material?
weight_outlier.pass: No sign of an unusual weight.
weight_outlier.fail: A reviewer confirmed this weight is out of line.
weight_outlier.warn: The weight is far from what this material usually weighs. Review the flag.

payout.label: What happened to the payout?
payout.unknown: No payout exists for this collection.

ledger_anchor.label: Is it on the ledger?
ledger_anchor.pass: Yes. It is entry number {seq} on the append-only chain.

fingerprint.label: Does the stored photo still match its signed fingerprint?
fingerprint.match: Yes. Your browser re-hashed the stored photo and it equals the fingerprint signed on the phone.
fingerprint.mismatch: No. The stored photo does not match its fingerprint. Treat this collection as suspect.
fingerprint.missing: The photo has not arrived, so there is nothing to compare.
fingerprint.error: The photo could not be fetched. Try again.

events.photoAlt: Photo of the {material} on the scale
events.photoMissing: The photo has not arrived yet.
events.photoGuide: The photo should show the waste, the scale and the scale's display.
events.ledgerHint: The entry hash links this collection into the chain. Verify the chain on the Ledger screen.

anomalies.title: Anomalies
anomalies.intro: Flags are notes for a person. They never block a payout. Confirm what is a real problem and dismiss what is not. A different admin may overturn your verdict.
anomalies.overturnHint: You cannot change your own verdict. Another admin can.

reconciliation.title: Reconciliation
reconciliation.intro: Kilograms collected against what the recycler accepted. This is the main check against inflated weights.
reconciliation.noRows: Nothing was collected or sold in this period.
reconciliation.saveHint: A saved report is never edited. Material over tolerance raises an anomaly flag.
reconciliation.recordSaleIntro: Enter what the recycler accepted. Attach the receipt photo if you have one. The sale is written to the ledger.
reconciliation.totalHint: Copy what the receipt says. It is never computed.
reconciliation.saleInvalid: Check the material, buyer, date and weights. Tare cannot exceed gross.

ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.intro: The append-only chain behind every collection, payout, authorization and refill. Each entry's hash includes the one before it, so a change anywhere breaks everything after it.
ledger.verifyOk: The chain is intact: {count} entries recomputed.
ledger.verifyFail: The chain is BROKEN at entry {seq}.
ledger.checkpointsVerified: {count, plural, one {# checkpoint matches the chain} other {# checkpoints match the chain}}
ledger.signaturesNotChecked: Not checked (no signing key configured here)
ledger.noCheckpoints: No checkpoint has been signed yet.
ledger.publicKeyHint: Write this down somewhere the operator cannot change. An auditor pins it to prove a checkpoint is ours.
ledger.outsiderIntro: An auditor needs no login. Export the ledger and run the standalone verifier on their own machine.
ledger.outsiderHint: See docs/LEDGER.md in the repository for the full guide.
ledger.noEntries: No entries of this type in the loaded range.

staff.title: Staff
staff.intro: Everyone who can sign in on the staff side. Accounts are created by the operator. Switching an account off signs that person out on their next request.
staff.selfNote: You cannot change your own account.
staff.deactivateConfirm: Switch off {name}? They will be signed out on their next request.

sessions.title: Session
sessions.activeHint: A new session is only scheduled. Supervisors can record collections only while the session is active and the time is inside its window.
sessions.closeConfirm: Close this session? Supervisors can no longer start new collections in it. Queued ones still sync.

rates.title: Rates
rates.intro: What each material pays per kilogram. A rate is never edited: a new rate closes the old one, and each collection is paid at the rate in force when it was recorded.
rates.setIntro: Applies from now. Collections already recorded keep the rate they were recorded with.
rates.invalid: Enter a material and a price greater than zero.

bar.signedOut: Signed out. {count} saved on this phone. Tap to sign in.
bar.needsAttention: {count, plural, one {# collection needs attention} other {# collections need attention}}. Tap to see why.

Sync.signedOutNow: You are signed out. Nothing is lost: your collections are saved on this phone and will send after you sign in.
Sync.serverUnreachable: The server could not be reached. Your collections are saved and will be tried again.
Sync.someNeedAttention: {count, plural, one {# collection was refused} other {# collections were refused}}. See why below.

reasons.content_hash_mismatch: This record changed after it was saved, so it cannot be trusted. Ask your hub lead.
reasons.invalid_timestamp: The time on this record is not valid.
reasons.collector_not_found: The server does not know this collector yet. Register the collector first, then try again.
reasons.collector_not_authorized: This collector is not authorized yet. Ask your hub lead to authorize them, then try again.
reasons.no_rate: There was no rate for this material at that time. Ask an admin.
reasons.rate_mismatch: The rate on this record was not the rate in force. Ask an admin.
reasons.supervisor_not_assigned: You were not assigned to this session. Ask an admin.
reasons.event_not_yours: This collection was recorded by someone else.
reasons.invalid_event: This record is not valid (for example the weight is too large). It cannot be sent as it is.
reasons.session_not_found: The session for this record was not found. Ask an admin.

reasons.future_timestamp: The clock on this phone was ahead of the real time. Check the phone's date and time.
reasons.invalid_data: The server could not store these values. Tell an admin.
